wave3_findings_and_repairs: D-20 broke cross-process determinism: parent-measured sandbox CPU made the same spec and seed give different event hashes in two new processes (157 of 1,795 events of a half-day population world; cpu_ms and cloud compute units, which feed cloud billing), so K1's cross-process resume could not continue with the uninterrupted run's hashes. Repair: sandbox.metering.DiskMemo - the deterministic memo's anchors are shared by every process of the machine (SQLite, first writer wins; the 3x + 1 ms tolerance rule and per-lineage keys unchanged); SandboxConfig.memo_path; worlds use metering.default_memo_path() ($CRUCIBLE_METER_MEMO, 'off' = per process; params.meter_memo='process' opts out). tests/test_v5_substrate_memo.py.

K2 tests failed after the merge: a world with an extra (observer) module or typed_events has another spec hash, hence another measurement lineage, and billed its sandboxed requests by fresh measurements. params.meter_lineage lets an experiment's arms share a lineage; the K2 tests give every arm the same lineage, and a new test shows that without it only ext/cloud.usage events differ (the measurement confound).

Fact scan: 3 unclassified wave-2 tables (pop_social.cols:pop, space.space_items, space_read.space_read_items) classified. Blind spot found and closed: columns of an owner's own column table were never scanned - pop.contacts (a fourth tie graph), pop.communities (memberships of their own) and the audience engine's creator follower sets (a third follow graph) were silent duplicates; every column is now scanned on its own name, and the three are on the allow-list with migrations; pop.wallet_cents reviewed (pre-ledger claim, deposited through bank.move); 'edge' signature fixed (matched 'knowledge').

Facts role 'legacy' (the migration target for 4.0 tables, which cannot be retired while 4.0 worlds must stay byte-identical): enforced on data in every world (facts.legacy_split) and certified by a named test (verified_by); a legacy table is not a known duplicate.
Mode C composition: initiators criterion (hub-and-spoke worlds refused).

Retention: periodic compaction was O(history) per call (19.3 s per weekly compact at day 365: collect re-read every cols.batch event of the log and every retained snapshot was unpickled for its roots and time); now incremental (batch refs cached in world.runtime with the last seq read) and snapshot metadata read once per process (snapshots are content-addressed by chain position).
Test isolation: tests/test_v5_substrate_modes.py loads the modules itself (one test failed when run alone).

Cross-process determinism of sandboxed work holds on one machine given the machine-level memo (first measurement wins); a fresh machine measures afresh, and a computation measured above 3x its anchor + 1 ms is billed fresh (honest, nondeterministic). Memo anchors are dropped beyond 2M rows (oldest first).

social/studio.py's own sandbox pool and rapid/engines/program_exec.py use the deterministic cost model with meter_scope None and no memo file: anchors shared by all worlds of a process, not across processes (owners C and H).

Snapshot bytes grow superlinearly (each snapshot holds the state, which keeps one artifacts metadata row per system blob: 222,702 rows after 365 days; 15 retained snapshots = 120 MB at day 365, growing 1.4 -> 3.3 MB/week). Blob and event growth rates are constant.

Historical runtime reconstruction (history.state_at(..., runtime=True)) is available only at times whose neural checkpoints are still stored: collect drops superseded checkpoints that no retained snapshot roots. State queries (runtime=False) stay exact at any time.

Wall time per simulated day grew 2.45 -> 4.49 s over 365 days; the weekly compaction was the main O(history) term (19.3 s at day 365); after the incremental fix a warm weekly compaction at day 372-379 takes 8.8-9.4 s (packing that week's blobs included), the remaining O(blobs) part being two blob-size scans (1.8 s); a full 365-day run was not repeated after the fix.
Fault injection still reaches few agent commands (random schema-valid commands rarely span modules); deliberate composed failures come from a labelled test driver module.
Cross-process exactness is verified on this machine (CPU torch), not across machines.
The event log is not bounded (linear, as any exact record); SQLite stores payloads > 2 KiB compressed, Postgres (JSON columns) does not.

Main-line isolation covers same-transaction subscribers. Couplings implemented as scheduled processes, or sharing kernel counters (unkeyed sched job ids), still shift later main-line positions; appliers that store an event's absolute seq in state (4.0 search_docs.seq) differ in that field when side events exist.

Bytes uploaded through the artifact.put tool are also in the recorded cmd event (arguments are recorded for regeneration); module code should store large media with artifacts.put, whose events hold only the REF.
A world moved to another store must run artifacts.export(world, dest_store) before it is loaded in another process.
integration_notes: BLOCKER for every population/civ world (integration fix): two kernel modules are named `space` (population/semantics.py Space with table space_keys, semantic/space/store.py SpaceRecords with table space_items); the population's space.recorded payload {keys, ref} reaches SpaceRecords.ap_recorded (KeyError: 'items'), so every pop.tick fails (94 proc.failed in 36 h of a population world) and civ.generate refuses ('miss dependencies [space]'). facts.REVIEWED classifies space.space_items; if the surviving module keeps space_keys instead, classify it (no shared-kind signature: private by default).

O (sandbox, D-20): sandbox/metering.py gains DiskMemo / default_memo_path / Memo.bill(disk=); runner.SandboxConfig.memo_path; services/code.py sandbox_pool passes memo_path in the deterministic cost model and honours params.meter_lineage / params.meter_memo; tenant (uid) stays per spec hash. O's unit tests use SandboxConfig() without memo_path and are unaffected. Keep these properties in any metering change: a new process must bill an identical computation of the same lineage exactly as the first measurement, or cross-process resume and replication break again.

C (social/studio.py) and H (rapid/engines/program_exec.py): pass meter_scope (world lineage) and memo_path=metering.default_memo_path() to SandboxConfig, or use code.sandbox_pool - today their anchors are shared across all worlds of a process and not across processes.

J (civ.counterfactual): arms created by forks share the measurement lineage; an arm that changes the spec must set params.meter_lineage to the factual world's lineage (services.code: params.meter_lineage or spec.hash()[:16]). Mode C composition now also needs >= 5 initiating sources.
